added: #Take off the radiator cap. Only do this when the engine is cool. This will release pressure on the cooling system and prevent vacuum lock when draining.<ref>https://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Replace-Your-Cars-Radiator-/10000000177633496/g.html</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 1 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Squeeze the radiator hoses. If you feel a crunching sensation when you squeeze the hoses you probably have rust in the cooling system. The system will need to be flushed before filling with new coolant. There are kits to do this at your local auto part store, but if you would rather, you can do it yourself.[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 2 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Place a drip pan under the petcock. It is imperative that you contain and control all coolant that you drain from your vehicle. Aside from being damaging to the environment, the coolant is highly toxic to humans and animals. Its sweet taste and smell make it attractive to children and pets and can result in serious injury or death.<ref>https://www.popularmechanics.com/cars/how-to/a5388/4345271/</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 3 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Open the petcock. You can use your hands or a pair of pliers to turn the pet cock. This will open it and allow coolant to drain into your drip pan.<ref>https://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Replace-Your-Cars-Radiator-/10000000177633496/g.html</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 4 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Flush the radiator. If you felt rust or if your coolant seems dirty, now is the appropriate time to flush your coolant. If you are unfamiliar with the procedure you can refer to [[Flush a Radiator]].[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 5 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Recycle all liquids captured. Liquids from the flush will also contain coolant. These liquids are considered hazardous waste and must not be poured into the ground. Check with your local recycling and waste management facilities for disposal options.<ref>https://www.popularmechanics.com/cars/how-to/a329/2063646/</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 6 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Remove the upper and lower radiator hose and the hose to the reservoir. This will require you to loosen the hose clamps. You do this by using a hose clamp remover or a pair of channel locks to squeeze the ends of the hose clamp together. Once the ends are together, the clamp should be loose enough to slide up the radiator hose, allowing you to remove the hose from the radiator.<ref>https://www.howacarworks.com/cooling-systems/how-to-remove-a-car-radiator</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 7 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Disconnect the transmission line. In some cars, there may be a transmission fluid cooler built into the radiator. If there are metal lines running to the radiator from the transmission, they will need to be removed using a wrench. There should be two lines. Also, be careful to catch the transmission fluid that leaks when you disconnect these lines.<ref>https://www.2carpros.com/articles/how-to-replace-a-car-radiator</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 8 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Remove all electrical wiring harness connections. Locate and disconnect the fan motor electrical connector. This is usually the only electrical connection, but double check to make sure.[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 9 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Disconnect the air conditioner condenser. The air conditioner condenser is often connected to the radiator. To remove the radiator, you will need to remove the condenser mounting bolts with a wrench. This allows the condenser to stay in the engine bay and keeps the refrigerant system closed.<ref>https://www.2carpros.com/articles/how-to-replace-a-car-radiator</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 10 Version 4.jpg|center]]

#Remove the bolts from the mounting brackets. Look at how your radiator is attached to your car. Usually there are braces bolted to the frame on top, and the bottom rests on rubber feet within an indentation.<ref>https://www.popularmechanics.com/cars/how-to/a5388/4345271/</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 11 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Remove the radiator from the car. There should be no hoses, electrical connectors, and it should have sufficient clearance to be removed. If not, study the layout and think before disassembling anything else. Some other components may need to be removed like a top engine mount or the battery tray, but usually the radiator is held in only by the mounting brackets.<ref>https://www.popularmechanics.com/cars/how-to/a5388/4345271/</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 12 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Disassemble the radiator. Once the radiator is out, you will need to look for any parts that need to be transferred over to the new radiator. This might include the fan shroud assembly, brackets, or other parts. Remove any such parts before recycling the radiator.<ref>https://www.2carpros.com/articles/how-to-replace-a-car-radiator</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 13 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Connect all parts to the radiator. Any parts that were removed from the old radiator, such as brackets, fan shroud, etc., need to be installed on the new radiator before it goes into the car.<ref>https://www.2carpros.com/articles/how-to-replace-a-car-radiator</ref>{{expertgreenbox:161715|''' Be sure to accurately measure your current radiator before buying a replacement.''' Use a tape measure to determine the radiator core's length, width, and depth. Also, note the number of core rows (horizontal channels) in the radiator. Aim to find a replacement with the same or more core rows to ensure optimal cooling efficiency.|}}[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 14 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Insert the radiator into the car. It will simply lower (or raise) into the same space that you took the old radiator out of. This part is fairly easy, but be cautious. If you bend the fins of the radiator you will need to straighten them out with a radiator comb to ensure proper airflow and cooling.<ref>https://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Replace-Your-Cars-Radiator-/10000000177633496/g.html</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 15 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Connect the mounting brackets. Lower or fit the radiator into the support track. Align the radiator with any mounting tabs, including any rubber mouldings between the radiator and the support rack. Tighten the mounting bracket bolts to secure the radiator in the engine bay.<ref>https://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Replace-Your-Cars-Radiator-/10000000177633496/g.html</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 16 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Secure the air conditioning condensor. Use the same condenser mounting bolts that your removed from the old radiator. Align the condenser so that the bolts fit into the radiator and screw them in with a wrench or ratchet.[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 17 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Plug in any wiring harnesses. This will restore power to your electric fan (if your car has an electric fan). If there are any other electrical components with your radiator, this will restore power to them as well.<ref>https://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Replace-Your-Cars-Radiator-/10000000177633496/g.html</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 18 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Connect the transmission coolant lines. This will ensure that your transmission keeps cool, and that transmission fluid isn’t leaked. Be sure not to cross thread these fittings, as that might result in a poor seal and leaking transmission fluid. Tighten with a wrench.<ref>https://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Replace-Your-Cars-Radiator-/10000000177633496/g.html</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 19 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Connect the upper and lower radiator hoses and the hose to the reservoir. This will complete your cooling system and allow coolant to flow into and out of your radiator. Slide the hoses onto their respective fittings at the top and bottom of the radiator. Then use a pair of channel locks to move the hose clamps up into place. This holds the hoses to the radiator snuggly.<ref>https://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Replace-Your-Cars-Radiator-/10000000177633496/g.html</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 20 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Verify that you have the correct coolant. You will need to consult your owner’s manual or service manual for proper coolant specifications.<ref>https://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Replace-Your-Cars-Radiator-/10000000177633496/g.html</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 21 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Dilute the coolant with distilled water. You can purchase pre-diluted coolant, or use distilled water to dilute the coolant. This allows the coolant to function properly, so be sure that you are diluting to the correct concentrations. This is usually a one to one dilution (half water, half coolant).<ref>https://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Replace-Your-Cars-Radiator-/10000000177633496/g.html</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 22 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Pour to the fill line. You should pour directly into the radiator until you see the fluid near the top, and then fill the reservoir tank to the cold fill line. You may need to add additional coolant once the engine circulates what you add.<ref>https://www.2carpros.com/articles/how-to-replace-a-car-radiator</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 23 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Bleed air pockets from the cooling system. Some cars require a specific routine to bleed air pockets out of the cooling system. Check your service manual for details on how to do this properly.<ref>https://www.carsdirect.com/car-repair/how-to-bleed-a-radiator-an-auto-diy-maintenance-guide</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 24 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Reinstall your radiator cap. This closes off your system and allows it to build pressure. You have now changed your radiator.<ref>https://www.2carpros.com/articles/how-to-replace-a-car-radiator</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 25 Version 2.jpg|center]]

Once the ends are together, the clamp should be loose enough to slide up the radiator hose, allowing you to remove the hose from the radiator.[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 5.jpg|center]]<ref>http://www.howacarworks.com/cooling-systems/how-to-remove-a-car-radiator</ref>

#Disconnect the transmission line. In some cars, there may be a transmission fluid cooler built into the radiator. If there are metal lines running to the radiator from the transmission, they will need to be removed using a wrench. There should be two lines. Also, be careful to catch the transmission fluid that leaks when you disconnect these lines.<ref>https://www.2carpros.com/articles/how-to-replace-a-car-radiator</ref>
#*These will be a set of two metal lines running into the bottom of the radiator. Do not bend or kink these lines.
#*The condenser mounting bolts are usually near the top corners of the radiator. You will not need to unhook any lines or hoses from the condenser.

#Secure the air conditioning condensor. Use the same condenser mounting bolts that your removed from the old radiator. Align the condenser so that the bolts fit into the radiator and screw them in with a wrench or ratchet.<ref>http://www.autozone.com/repairinfo/repairguide/repairGuideContent.jsp?pageId=0996b43f802c62ec</ref>

#Connect the transmission coolant lines. This will ensure that your transmission keeps cool, and that transmission fluid isn’t leaked. Be sure not to crossthread these fittings, as that might result in a poor seal and leaking transmission fluid. Tighten with a wrench.<ref>http://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Replace-Your-Cars-Radiator-/10000000177633496/g.html</ref>
#*It is likely that there will be gaskets that fit between these lines and the radiator. Be sure that the gasket did not get left on your old radiator.

#Connect the upper and lower radiator hoses and the hose to the reservoir. This will complete your cooling system and allow coolant to flow into and out of your radiator. Slide the hoses onto their respective fittings at the top and bottom of the radiator. Then use a pair of channel locks to move the hose clamps up into place. This holds the hoses to the radiator snuggly.<ref>http://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Replace-Your-Cars-Radiator-/10000000177633496/g.html</ref>
*You should replace any hoses that are cracked, worn, or punctured. You should also replace any hoses that haven’t been replaced in the past 60,000 miles.
*Replace any of the wire/screw type clamps with hose clamps.

added: ==Steps==
===Draining and Flushing the Cooling System===

#Take off the radiator cap. Only do this when the engine is cool. This will release pressure on the cooling system and prevent vacuum lock when draining.<ref>http://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Replace-Your-Cars-Radiator-/10000000177633496/g.html</ref>

#Squeeze the radiator hoses. If you feel a crunching sensation when you squeeze the hoses you probably have rust in the cooling system. The system will need to be flushed before filling with new coolant. There are kits to do this at your local auto part store, but if you would rather, you can do it yourself.[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 2.jpg|center]]

#Place a drip pan under the petcock. It is imperative that you contain and control all coolant that you drain from your vehicle. Aside from being damaging to the environment, the coolant is highly toxic to humans and animals. Its sweet taste and smell make it attractive to children and pets and can result in serious injury or death.<ref>http://www.popularmechanics.com/cars/how-to/a5388/4345271/</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 4.jpg|center]]

#Open the petcock. You can use your hands or a pair of pliers to turn the pet cock. This will open it and allow coolant to drain into your drip pan.<ref>http://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Replace-Your-Cars-Radiator-/10000000177633496/g.html</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 3Bullet1.jpg|center]]

#Flush the radiator. If you felt rust or if your coolant seems dirty, now is the appropriate time to flush your coolant. If you are unfamiliar with the procedure you can refer to [[Flush a Radiator]].[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 3Bullet5.jpg|center]]

#Recycle all liquids captured. Liquids from the flush will also contain coolant. These liquids are considered hazardous waste and must not be poured into the ground. Check with your local recycling and waste management facilities for disposal options.<ref>http://www.popularmechanics.com/cars/how-to/a329/2063646/</ref>
===Disconnecting the Radiator===

#Remove the upper and lower radiator hose. This will require you to loosen the hose clamps. You do this by using a hose clamp remover or a pair of channel locks to squeeze the ends of the hose clamp together. Once the ends are together, the clamp should be loose enough to slide up the radiator hose, allowing you to remove the hose from the radiator.[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 5.jpg|center]]<ref>http://www.howacarworks.com/cooling-systems/how-to-remove-a-car-radiator</ref>

#*Some older models may have a screw type clamp. For this you will need a socket or screwdriver to twist the screw on the hose clamp. Counterclockwise should loosen and clockwise should tighten the clamp.

#Disconnect the transmission line. In some cars, there may be a transmission fluid cooler built into the radiator. If there are hoses running from the radiator from the transmission, they will need to be removed using a wrench. There should be two lines. Also, be careful to catch the transmission fluid that leaks when you disconnect these lines.<ref>https://www.2carpros.com/articles/how-to-replace-a-car-radiator</ref>
#*Be aware that the transmission fluid is also toxic and should be appropriately disposed of.

#Remove all electrical wiring harness connections. Locate and disconnect the fan motor electrical connector. This is usually the only electrical connection, but double check to make sure.[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 6.jpg|center]]

#Disconnect the air conditioner condenser. The air conditioner condenser is often connected to the radiator. To remove the radiator, you will need to remove the condenser mounting bolts with a wrench. This allows the condenser to stay in the engine bay and keeps the refrigerant system closed.<ref>https://www.2carpros.com/articles/how-to-replace-a-car-radiator</ref>

#Remove the bolts from the mounting brackets. Look at how your radiator is attached to your car. Usually there are braces bolted to the frame on top, and the bottom rests on rubber feet within an indentation.<ref>http://www.popularmechanics.com/cars/how-to/a5388/4345271/</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 7.jpg|center]]

#Remove the radiator from the car. There should be no hoses, electrical connectors, and it should have sufficient clearance to be removed. If not, study the layout and think before disassembling anything else. Some other components may need to be removed like a top engine mount or the battery tray, but usually the radiator is held in only by the mounting brackets.<ref>http://www.popularmechanics.com/cars/how-to/a5388/4345271/</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 8.jpg|center]]

#Disassemble the radiator. Once the radiator is out, you will need to look for any parts that need to be transferred over to the new radiator. This might include the fan shroud assembly, brackets, or other parts. Remove any such parts before recycling the radiator.<ref>https://www.2carpros.com/articles/how-to-replace-a-car-radiator</ref>
===Installing the New Radiator===

#Connect all parts to the radiator. Any parts that were removed from the old radiator, such as brackets, fan shroud, etc., need to be installed on the new radiator before it goes into the car.<ref>https://www.2carpros.com/articles/how-to-replace-a-car-radiator</ref>

#Insert the radiator into the car. It will simply lower (or raise) into the same space that you took the old radiator out of. This part is fairly easy, but be cautious. If you bend the fins of the radiator you will need to straighten them out with a radiator comb to ensure proper airflow and cooling.<ref>http://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Replace-Your-Cars-Radiator-/10000000177633496/g.html</ref>

#Connect the mounting brackets. Lower or fit the radiator into the support track. Align the radiator with any mounting tabs, including any rubber mouldings between the radiator and the support rack. Tighten the mounting bracket bolts to secure the radiator in the engine bay.<ref>http://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Replace-Your-Cars-Radiator-/10000000177633496/g.html</ref>

#Secure the air conditioning condensor. Use the same condenser mounting bolts that your removed from the old radiator. Align the condenser so that the bolts fit into the radiator and screw them in with a wrench or ratchet.<ref>http://www.autozone.com/repairinfo/repairguide/repairGuideContent.jsp?pageId=0996b43f802c62ec</ref>

#Plug in any wiring harnesses. This will restore power to your electric fan (if your car has an electric fan). If there are any other electrical components with your radiator, this will restore power to them as well.<ref>http://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Replace-Your-Cars-Radiator-/10000000177633496/g.html</ref>

#Connect the transmission coolant hose. This will ensure that your transmission keeps cool, and that transmission fluid isn’t leaked. Be sure not to crossthread these fittings, as that might result in a poor seal and leaking transmission fluid. Tighten with a wrench.<ref>http://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Replace-Your-Cars-Radiator-/10000000177633496/g.html</ref>

#Connect the upper and lower radiator hoses. This will complete your cooling system and allow coolant to flow into and out of your radiator. Slide the hoses onto their respective fittings at the top and bottom of the radiator. Then use a pair of channel locks to move the hose clamps up into place. This holds the hoses to the radiator snuggly.<ref>http://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Replace-Your-Cars-Radiator-/10000000177633496/g.html</ref>
===Refilling the Cooling System===

#Verify that you have the correct coolant. You will need to consult your owner’s manual or service manual for proper coolant specifications.<ref>http://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Replace-Your-Cars-Radiator-/10000000177633496/g.html</ref>

#Dilute the coolant with distilled water. You can purchase pre-diluted coolant, or use distilled water to dilute the coolant. This allows the coolant to function properly, so be sure that you are diluting to the correct concentrations. This is usually a one to one dilution (half water, half coolant).<ref>http://www.ebay.com/gds/How-to-Replace-Your-Cars-Radiator-/10000000177633496/g.html</ref>

#Pour to the fill line. You should pour directly into the radiator until you see the fluid near the top, and then fill the reservoir tank to the cold fill line. You may need to add additional coolant once the engine circulates what you add.<ref>https://www.2carpros.com/articles/how-to-replace-a-car-radiator</ref>[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 10.jpg|center]]

#Bleed air pockets from the cooling system. Some cars require a specific routine to bleed air pockets out of the cooling system. Check your service manual for details on how to do this properly.<ref>http://www.carsdirect.com/car-repair/how-to-bleed-a-radiator-an-auto-diy-maintenance-guide</ref>

#Reinstall your radiator cap. This closes off your system and allows it to build pressure. You have now changed your radiator.<ref>https://www.2carpros.com/articles/how-to-replace-a-car-radiator</ref>
==Tips==
*If it is indeed necessary, read how to lift your car [[Use Jack Stands|here]].
*Use penetrating oil on any hard to turn bolts. This will help prevent breaking and stripping.
*A Haynes or Chilton manual would be helpful.

#  Notice if you have rust in the cooling system. If you feel a crunching sensation when you squeeze the hoses you probably have rust in the cooling system. The system will need to be [[Flush a Radiator|flushed]] before filling with new coolant. There are kits to do this at your local auto part store, but if you would rather do it yourself follow this procedure:
#*Drain old coolant into appropriate container for disposal.(most radiators have a drain plug on the bottom)[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 3Bullet1.jpg|center]]
#*Locate and remove the thermostat.[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 3Bullet2.jpg|center]]
#*Locate and remove the upper coolant hose.[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 3Bullet3.jpg|center]]
#*Insert garden hose into where upper coolant hose enters engine.[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 3Bullet4.jpg|center]]
#*Turn on hose, run until water exiting system is clear.[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 3Bullet5.jpg|center]]
#* Remove the coolant reservoir and flush it with water.[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 3Bullet6.jpg|center]]
#*Drain all water and re-install thermostat and reservoir.[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 3Bullet7.jpg|center]]

#  Drain old coolant into appropriate container for disposal if you haven't already done so and remove the thermostat. Most radiators have a drain plug on the bottom.[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 4.jpg|center]]

#  Locate and disconnect all hoses leading to radiator. Use penetrating oil on all hose clamps to avoid breakage/stripping. In some cars, there may be a transmission fluid cooler built into the radiator. If there are hoses running from the radiator from the transmission, be careful to catch the trans fluid that drops when you disconnect those lines (don't reuse that fluid either). Be careful with all fluids as they are very toxic.[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 5.jpg|center]]

#  Locate and disconnect the fan motor electrical connector and any other electrical connectors. Usually it is necessary to remove the fan assembly in order to remove the radiator. It should be bolted to the radiator directly. Use penetrating oil on bolts to avoid stripping/breakage![[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 6.jpg|center]]

#  Look at your radiator. There should be no hoses, electrical connectors, and it should have sufficient clearance to be removed. If not, study the layout and think before disassembling anything else. Some other components may need to be removed like a top engine mount or the battery tray.[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 7.jpg|center]]

#  Look at how your radiator is attached to your car. Usually there are braces bolted to the frame on top, and the bottom rests on rubber feet within an indentation. Remove the top braces (Use penetrating oil on bolts to avoid stripping/breakage!) and pull upwards on the radiator. If it comes out, congratulations! If not, don't yank or pry. Study it and find the other bolts.[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 8.jpg|center]]
#*Some radiators and fans are removed as an assembly. Some also may require the a/c condenser be disconnected before the radiator can be removed.

#  Remember that installation is the reverse of disassemble. Remember not to over tighten hose clamps. Go over everything you took off in your head! If you forget the fan motor connector or a tiny water pump bypass hose you can waste a lot of effort and time.[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 9.jpg|center]]

# Refill the cooling system with coolant when everything has been assembled. To do this, remove the cap from the radiator, fill until coolant is visible but a few inches below cap level. Start the engine (don't rev or accelerate); the coolant level will lower as the engine sucks in coolant. Continue to fill with coolant until the level stabilizes then install and tighten the cap. Lastly, fill the coolant reservoir with coolant to the appropriate level. If transmission fluid was spilled, check trans fluid level and add new trans fluid if necessary.[[Image:Change a Car Radiator Step 10.jpg|center]]
# *Some engines have a special fill procedure or bleeding air out procedure. Follow the manufacturer recommendations for refilling.
